item.title: Early alerts, simple journeys and a stress-free experience: What passengers want at airports
item.description: ACI World’s 2027 global traveller survey found that while 77% of passengers leave airports with ‘positive emotions’, they are seeking seamless journeys and want to be kept in the loop about potential disruptions.

item.title: Xi Jinping greets Trump with a hug and red carpet at Shenzhen airport
item.description: Donald Trump arrives in Shenzhen, China, ahead of a trilateral summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, with Ukraine and nuclear security on the agenda.

item.title: 'Human': Cambridge Dictionary's Word of the Year 2026 tackles ongoing AI fears
item.description: Amid the global and controversial debate surrounding artificial intelligence in daily life, Cambridge Dictionary has crowned “human” as its Word of the Year for 2026.

item.title: Germany cuts energy tax and extends fuel price cap in 2027
item.description: Families could save around €8 a month, as Berlin also renews its commitment to keep petrol affordable.

item.title: Drug that mimics Viagra shows promise as Alzheimer's treatment
item.description: Experts said the results are encouraging, but that more research is needed before the drug is offered to patients.

item.title: Carney warns lack of global governance on AI an ‘enormous risk’
item.description: Canada’s Prime Minister cited economic, biohazard, democratic and human dignity risks associated with unregulated artificial intelligence.

item.title: Amazon's Jeff Bezos, RFK Jr and Hollywood celebrities comment on Robert Pattinson casting as James Bond
item.description: “Welcome to His Majesty’s Secret Service, Mr Bond.” From Amazon boss Jeff Bezos to Brad Pitt via some of Robert Pattinson's former co-stars, here's the lowdown on the reactions to the seventh 007.

item.title: Cheers and reactions in Alaska after Mary Peltola's Senate win
item.description: Democrat Mary Peltola has defeated Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan in Alaska's closely fought Senate race, securing a political comeback in a state that has repeatedly backed Donald Trump.

item.title: Dubai's businesses gain an AI workforce on demand
item.description: Dubai launches Chamber AI Hub, the first chamber-led agentic AI marketplace, with ready-made agents and training to help companies transform operations.

item.title: Xi and Putin meet ahead of planned summit with Trump
item.description: Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin meet in Shenzhen ahead of a rare trilateral summit with Donald Trump, focusing on energy, finance and global security.

item.title: War is accelerating Ukraine's AI rollout, digital chief tells Euronews
item.description: The need to keep essential public services running during Russia’s war has accelerated Ukraine’s adoption of artificial intelligence, offering lessons for Europe, the country’s chief AI officer told Euronews.

item.title: Where is Caroline? A young woman disappeared in the German mountains, no trace of her for weeks
item.description: Carolin Schmidt has been missing since 6 September 2026. Last seen around Mittenwald and Garmisch-Partenkirchen on hikes near the Bavaria–Tyrol border. No trace of her for over ten weeks.

item.title: 007 set-jetting: Iconic James Bond filming locations around Europe you can visit
item.description: From the Scottish scenery of Skyfall to the Monte Carlo casino in GoldenEye, here’s all the places in Europe to add to your must-visit list ahead of the next Bond movie in 2028.

item.title: Apple outage hits App Store, becoming the latest casualty of major cyber breakdowns
item.description: An update gone awry at Apple follows a rash of major outages in recent days, including problems affecting the Federal Aviation Administration, United Airlines and Microsoft.

item.title: Human resources: Stop buying talent, start building it
item.description: Paul Hamilton is founder of Halo Service Solutions, a UK software company that has built its workforce around graduates, degree apprentices and other early-career talent. He argues why businesses must stop competing for experienced candidates and start investing in developing the next generation.

item.title: Black Friday deals under scrutiny as Portuguese watchdog warns
item.description: As the discount season begins, Portugal’s DECO PROteste warns that some items in Black Friday promotions were cheaper before the sales began. The consumer group urges shoppers to check price histories and plan purchases.

item.title: Can you survive 72 hours? The EU wants you to prepare an emergency plan
item.description: The European Commission wants households to cover basic needs for at least 72 hours if a crisis disrupts essential services. Watch the video!

item.title: Europe and Jordan: A strategic partnership for prosperity and a stable Middle East
item.description: 'European investors, together with Jordanian businesses', can create economic value. Emphasise Dubravka Šuica, European Commissioner for the Mediterranean, and Tareq Abu Ghazaleh, Jordan's Minister of Investment in an exclusive piece for Euronews. Jordan could be Europe’s gateway to the Middle East.

item.title: Thousands rally in Slovakia against PM Robert Fico perceived as too pro-Russia
item.description: Fico, who opposes military aid to Ukraine and maintains close relations with Russian President Vladimir Putin, has repeatedly clashed with the European Union during his current term.

item.title: Eurobonds are back as Brussels unveils new support loan for Ukraine
item.description: Good morning! It's Wednesday, and my name is Jorge Liboreiro, ready to crunch numbers. Why? Because today is all about financial support for Ukraine, which is becoming harder to pin down. Let's break it down.

item.title: Europe Today: Crimean bridge, French presidential elections and Serbian Students List
item.description: Ukrainian forces used drones and missiles to strike the road and railway sections of the Crimean Bridge. France presidential election race is already taking shape and we speak with Willy Nyeko, Emergency Coordinator in Gaza for the UN World Food Programme.

item.title: Haiti formalises security pact with El Salvador as thousands march in support of Bukele
item.description: In the first 10 months of 2026, the UN recorded 4,595 deaths and 2,050 injuries to armed violence in Haiti.

item.title: Beyond The Streets: Inside London's major exhibition celebrating six decades of street culture
item.description: From Goldie’s drum ’n’ bass record room to a surreal puppet shop, BEYOND THE STREETS brings six decades of street culture into one of London’s most prestigious art spaces.

item.title: From detourists to beekeeping: Five ‘hidden’ travel trends for 2027
item.description: Seeking out lesser-known neighbourhoods, booking beekeeping experiences, and learning a local game while on holiday are among the hidden trends set to shape travel in 2027.

item.title: World of Warcraft's virtual 'Corrupted Blood' pandemic became a model for real epidemics
item.description: In 2005, a programming error unleashed a plague in World of Warcraft that epidemiologists used to study people's behaviour during an outbreak, later revived by COVID-19.

item.title: Democrat Mary Peltola unseats Republican and flips US Senate seat in tight race in Alaska
item.description: Democrats will control 56 seats in the 100-seat Senate which will give them the power to block legislation, launch broad investigations into Trump's administration and thwart his judicial and senior government appointments.

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO price is due today. What should investors know?
item.description: The Claude maker is expected to set its IPO price on Wednesday before a Nasdaq debut on Thursday. Retail investors in France, Germany and other European markets can apply through participating brokers.

item.title: Irish man charged with 'effectively' destroying US military C-130 aircraft at Shannon Airport
item.description: Daithi O’Corrain, described by supporters as an independent peace activist, was arrested immediately after the attack by Ireland's police force, An Garda Síochána.

item.title: South America’s lithium fields and Indonesia’s nickel pits reveal the dark side of electrification
item.description: German aerial photographer Tom Hegen has documented the energy transition from Chile’s lithium-rich Atacama Desert to the nickel-processing complexes of Sulawesi, Indonesia.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 18th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 18th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Google’s Ask Maps expands to 30 European countries – here’s how it works for travel planning
item.description: Holiday planning has been given an AI-powered upgrade. Google’s Ask Maps platform has expanded to Europe, helping travellers turn saved places and road trip ideas into handy itineraries.

item.title: East-Central Europe hit by more than 50 non-traditional security incidents since October
item.description: More and more disruptive events that are not classic military actions are occurring, yet they continue to threaten our security, from state-sponsored cyberattacks to climate change and global pandemics.

item.title: China's Xi and Russia's Putin hold talks on eve of three-way summit with Trump
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are holding talks in Shenzhen, a day before a first-of-its-kind trilateral summit with US President Donald Trump in the southern Chinese city.

item.title: Nvidia beats forecasts and rules out Huang’s return as CEO
item.description: Nvidia reported better-than-expected results, raised its forecast for next fiscal year and said it had no plans to bring back co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO.

item.title: Europe risks returning to ‘pre-antibiotic era’ amid growing threat of drug-resistant superbugs
item.description: Antibiotic resistance is rising across Europe, with some countries facing sharper increases and fewer treatment options as experts call for stronger prevention and more responsible antibiotic use.

item.title: US criticises Ukraine's 'deep strike' campaign against Russia
item.description: German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius called the US' warning "quite a stupid thing," while his British counterpart Wes Streeting said there was "no doubt" in his mind that Ukraine's long-range strikes had "helped to degrade Putin's war machine."

item.title: Five viral moments from Pope Leo XIV's South American tour
item.description: Pope Leo XIV's South American tour brought several memorable moments, from an unexpected encounter with a flying rosary bracelet to a helicopter journey into Peru's remote Andes.

item.title: GTA 6: What to know about the upcoming Grand Theft Auto game
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI is generating huge excitement across Asia, despite restrictions on sales, censorship and the dominance of mobile gaming. While the game is not officially licensed in mainland China and faces content restrictions in Japan, fans are finding ways to access the franchise.

item.title: Dead Melbourne Cup racehorse found dumped in Sydney waste facility
item.description: REC Equine Specialists said So You Are had been euthanised before being collected by a "contracted provider" and taken to a "licensed landfill." The practice has apologised and said the horse should have been "promptly and respectfully buried."

item.title: US strikes targets in Qeshm Island after Iranian mines hit five ships in Hormuz
item.description: Iran says the US military carried out several attacks on Qeshm Island in southern Iran, while at least five ships were set on fire by mines in the Strait of Hormuz earlier in the day.

item.title: Russia cannot have a say over NATO's military activities, Norwegian foreign minister warns
item.description: Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide told Euronews that Moscow must not be allowed to dictate Europe's security arrangements while also warning against a return to spheres of influence.

item.title: French foreign minister slams Lavrov accusations about 'direct participation' in Ukraine war
item.description: Russia said on Tuesday it was aware of French troops deployed to Ukraine, calling it "direct participation" in the war and saying a message had been issued to Paris. France has rejected the claim troops are directly involved in fighting as "absurd."

item.title: EU climate chief Hoekstra: Electrification key for Europe to compete with China as COP pushes global target
item.description: Hoekstra tells On the Record that electrification is key to Europe's industrial competitiveness, as COP talks push for a global target of 35% by 2035.

item.title: EU economy chief Dombrovskis warns France to rein in debt as growth outlook improves
item.description: EU economy chief Dombrovskis warns France to rein in debt as growth outlook improves

item.title: New anti-regime protests erupt in flashpoint Iranian city
item.description: A protest sparked by a deadly bus crash in a western Iranian city turned into a new anti-regime protest with hundreds chanting "Death to the dictator."

item.title: Moldova closes airspace after 'Shahed-type' drone detected heading towards Chișinău
item.description: "Russia's war threatens all of Europe," President Maia Sandu wrote in a post on social media, adding that "several Russian drones" had violated Moldovan airspace on Tuesday.

item.title: All 19 crew members rescued after gas carrier 'struck' in Black Sea off Bulgaria
item.description: It marks the latest in a string of similar incidents in the Black Sea believed to be linked to Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

item.title: Euronews Verify: What's at stake as Europe seeks to triple its data centre capacity?
item.description: Europe wants to triple its data centre capacity, but residents and environmental campaigners are taking to the streets to demand a pause on new data centre projects. Why? And what’s at stake?

item.title: Beyond the green premium: Competitive advantage through decarbonization
item.description: 'The opportunities that decarbonization offers have never been greater', explains Noam Boussidan, Head of the First Movers Coalition, in an op-ed for Euronews. In stable conditions, fossil-based inputs may look cheaper, but that advantage is quickly lost when supply is disrupted or prices spike.

item.title: Europe Tonight: Eurozone growth forecast at 1.2%, Ukraine strikes Crimea bridge
item.description: The EU forecasts 1.2% Eurozone growth amid inflation and debt concerns, analysed live tonight by Valdis Dombrovskis. Meanwhile, Ukraine strikes a key Russia-Crimea bridge ahead of talks with Norway's Foreign Minister, and Spain's Pedro Sánchez slams EU Rwanda asylum plans.
